types.name: bug
types.description: Something that exists does not work as intended

types.name: enhancement
types.description: A new feature, or a change to how something works

types.name: question
types.description: Asks how something works or whether something is possible

types.name: documentation
types.description: The docs are missing, wrong or unclear

areas.area:data: Dataset management: data add/import/list/validate/split, train.jsonl and valid.jsonl
areas.area:train: Fine-tuning with MLX: LoRA parameters, training runs, checkpoints, training logs
areas.area:export: Fusing adapters and exporting models: GGUF conversion, quantisation, llama.cpp
areas.area:chat: Chatting with a fine-tuned model: nanotune chat, llama-server lifecycle
areas.area:benchmark: Benchmarks and judges: tests.json, match modes, judge providers and API keys, reports
areas.area:cli: Project setup and CLI surface: init, status, clean, config.json, flags, the TUI, model downloads and the toolchain

flags.performance: Speed, memory use or disk use is the substance of the issue
flags.security: A security weakness or hardening (e.g. API key handling)
flags.good first issue: Small, well-specified and self-contained: a newcomer could fix it from the issue alone

proposalGuidance: A proposal is a speculative idea, a design exploration or an 'is there interest in…' post: something to discuss rather than something anyone has committed to build. Concrete, clearly scoped features — a new flag, a new subcommand, a fix to how an existing step behaves — are not proposals, however large.
scopeGuidance: Nanotune is a simple interactive CLI for fine-tuning small language models on Apple Silicon with MLX and llama.cpp. Out of scope: training on other hardware backends (CUDA, ROCm) as built-in support, hosted or cloud training services, full pre-training of large models, and requests to bundle or endorse a specific commercial product. Integrations with experiment trackers or serving tools are in scope when they stay optional.
